text:
maria: Heads up — after merging the adaptive-batcher warmup patch we see a reproducible ~7-10% p99 regression on short prompts (seq ~256-512). I ran an nsys capture and a perfetto timeline; attaching links. Any ideas on kernel hopping or memcopy spikes?

nsys: gs://redwood-traces/nsys/1777777000-adaptive-warmup-raw.qdrep
perfetto: https://perfetto.dev/trace/1777777000-warmup

ashwin: I pulled the nsys file and did a quick summary. There's a sharp jump in kernel launch frequency right after the warmup window completes. Two kernels alternate a lot: FastMatmul_Fused (short) and FastMatmul_Tiled (long). Launch counts in a 30s window:
```
KernelName, launches
FastMatmul_Fused, 15498
FastMatmul_Tiled, 15240
memcpyHtoD, 780
memcpyDtoH, 1320
```
The tiled kernel has larger per-launch variance; the hopping causes tail latency. Looks like the selector is flipping based on transient seq-length/stride signals.

kevin: corroborating logs from runner show KV cache churn around the same timestamps — eviction pressure increases when the selector swaps kernels. Snip from runner.log:
```
[2026-06-21T15:02:04Z] kv_cache: evicting 24 entries (owner=adaptive-batcher)
[2026-06-21T15:02:04Z] kernel_selector: selected FastMatmul_Tiled for model: redwood-v1 seq:512
[2026-06-21T15:02:04Z] kv_cache: warmup_alloc hit=0 miss=24
[2026-06-21T15:02:04Z] kernel_selector: fallback to FastMatmul_Fused
```
If the kernel change triggers different memory layouts for KV, we get extra D2H/H2D copies while the runtime re-binds caches. That matches the memcopy spike in perfetto.

lisa: I ran a bisect over the last week. Culprit commit is 0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7 ("adaptive-batcher: enable warmup heuristic and dynamic kernel probe"). Repro steps I used: 
```
# on perf cluster
./tools/loadgen --model redwood-v1 --seq 512 --tokens 50 --qps 120 --duration 300 --record-trace ./out.qdrep
nsys profile -o out.nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda -- ./bin/infer --config cfg.json
```
Bisect landed cleanly on that commit; earlier commits don't reproduce.

maria: Thanks — that aligns with what I saw. Perfetto slice shows memcpyDtoH ramp at t=00:01:22 then kernel stalls for ~12ms more often. I suspect the warmup heuristic toggles a probe that causes the selector to evaluate two candidate kernels every N requests, and the probing path does additional synchronization. Lowering the probe frequency or ensuring probes use a cheaper fallback should help.

ashwin: Proposal: change kernel-selector to prefer the "stable" kernel for X requests after a probe, and run probes off-thread so we don't stall the request path. Minimal patch (pseudo):
```
+if (probe_hit) {
+  schedule_probe_async(candidate);
+  current_kernel = last_stable_kernel;
+} else {
+  current_kernel = choose_based_on_stats();
+}
```
If we can keep probes off the critical path, the KV cache won't be re-bound mid-request.

kevin: I pushed a hotfix branch that forces stable kernel sticky for 60s: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8915. I ran a quick perf run with that branch and saw p99 back to baseline in my microbench. Risk: may mask legitimate kernel upgrades but it's safe as a narrow rollout.

eng-ci-bot: bisect job finished: culprit commit 0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7 identified. Artifact: gs://redwood-ci/bisect/1777777000/result.txt

maria: Good. I'll prepare a canary rollout of kevin's sticky-kernel patch to dedicated-blue for 2h and gather traces. If stable, we'll merge and follow up with a better async-probe implementation. I'll post perfetto/nsys after the canary. :thumbsup:
